title: Support season-scoped turnpoint changes for trophies
description:
Some trophies have had their turning points tweaked over time (e.g. a TP retired, moved, or swapped for a nearby one). Today each trophy in trophies.config.ts hardcodes a single TP set, e.g. Gransden Trophy: ["filter", "task.turnpoints", "<=>", ["BUG", "MEN"]]. When a trophy's TPs change we can only pick one set, so either the current season scores against stale TPs or historical seasons are silently re-scored against TPs that did not exist then — the historical winners shown for past seasons become wrong.

Need a way to declare that a given TP set (and the matching description/distance text) applies only from a given season onwards, keeping earlier seasons on the earlier definition.
design:
Sketch (to be validated during design, not settled):

Introduce a per-trophy archive of season-scoped variants rather than mutating the trophy in place. Something like an optional `variants` array on FlightTrophy, each entry carrying `fromSeason`/`toSeason` (inclusive, open-ended at either end) plus the fields that differ — at minimum `expr`, very likely `description` too, since descriptions name the TPs and the task distance ("Burley Gate (BUG) and Mendlesham Mast (MEN) - 507km").

Resolution: a lookup that, given a trophy + the resolved season, returns the effective trophy definition. Applied once where trophies are read for evaluation/display so trophyEval() and the UI stay season-agnostic. Season already flows through the app as the ?season= query param resolved in useFlights.ts.

Open questions:
- Do variants override whole `expr` or patch individual filters? Whole-expr is simpler and more explicit; patching avoids duplicating the 4-5 boilerplate filters every trophy shares.
- Overlapping/gapping ranges: validate at load, or trust the config?
- Does the same mechanism want to cover LadderTrophy, or is it flight-only for now?
- src/lib/turnpoints.ts (the TP code -> name/coords lookup) may also need historical entries if a retired TP code disappears from it.
acceptance_criteria:
- A trophy can declare more than one TP set, each bounded by season.
- Viewing a past season scores that season against the TPs in force then; viewing the current season uses the current TPs.
- Trophy description shown for a past season matches that season's TPs and distance.
- Trophies with no variants behave exactly as today (no config churn for the majority).
- Tests cover: season before the change, season after the change, and the boundary season itself.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/season-scoped-turnpoints: season-scoped trophy history + turnpoint lifecycle metadata

title: Validate DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL vs /api/flights before backend swap
description: De-risk trophies-grb/xeh: build the new JSON fetch+map (DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL -> Flight[]) and a comparison script that runs BOTH json-derived and csv-derived flights through the scoring engine, diffing trophy winners per season + raw Flight fields. Report which trophies match and which fields the JSON lacks (informs whether FLIGHT/{id} enrichment / trophies-ouv is needed alongside grb).
notes: FINDING (field + config analysis, decisive): DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL bulk JSON is LESS complete than the CSV. It provides: Forename/Surname, Glider/Registration(full G-reg), ClaimType, TP1-4/Start/Finish, Weekend/Junior/Height/TwoSeater flags, Site, ScoringDistance, XCPoints, Speed, HandicapSpeed. It is MISSING: Handicap, Completed, Declared, TaskAchievement, HandicapDistance, HeightLoss, the Open-ladder flag, and local1-5 (club) ladder flags. CSV has all of these. Impact on trophies: only weekend/junior/height (+open, since open=ALL flights in CSV) ladder trophies are reproducible from DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL alone (~Glass Jug, Pot Pewter Pringle). Broken: local-ladder trophies (Presidents=local1, Ted Warner=local5, Shark, Bolly...) and most flight trophies (need isCompleted/isDeclared/handicap/taskDistance -> Mug Metal Machin, Jubilee Bowl, Pons Pot, Kelman, A.L.L. Alexander, etc.). Only FLIGHT/{id} has everything (LocalLadder1-5, Handicap, Declared, TaskDistance) but costs ~1 req/flight (~hundreds/season). KEY: removing the backend (xeh) does NOT require JSON — the client can fetch the COMPLETE CSV directly (CORS confirmed). So xeh and grb are separable; grb (CSV->DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL) looks not worth it.
close_reason: Done. Conclusion: DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL alone can't reproduce the trophies (field-gap analysis decisive); CSV is the most complete single-request source. Decision: keep CSV, do backend removal (xeh) with client-side CSV fetch. No comparison harness needed.

title: Remove /api/flights backend; fetch BGA CSV directly client-side
description: The /api/flights Next API route is a thin proxy: CORS workaround, multi-year fan-out (start..end), CSV->JSON parse (papaparse), and Cache-Control headers. There is NO SSR anywhere in the app, so this route is the only server-side feature. Verified the BGA CSV endpoint already supports cross-origin browser calls (it reflects the Origin header and sets access-control-allow-credentials), so the proxy is unnecessary. Plan: move the fetch into useFlights (Promise.all over the 3 years), run parseCsv/papaparse client-side, delete src/pages/api/flights.ts (and csv.ts/flightCsvSpec.ts move to src/lib), drop axios in favour of fetch, update tests. Result: app becomes a pure static SPA hostable on GitHub Pages/Cloudflare. Trade-off: lose shared server-side caching (each visitor hits BGA directly, ~3 requests) — negligible for club traffic; URL/club code already public (no auth).
notes:
CORS evidence (2026-06-22): GET api.bgaladder.net/api/getlogfilescsv/2024/CGC with Origin header returns access-control-allow-origin reflecting the origin + access-control-allow-credentials: true.
API investigation (2026-06-22, via playwright). The BGA SPA uses a JSON API (all endpoints CORS-enabled — reflect Origin). Club code is CAM (not CGC). Relevant endpoints:
1. /API/DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL?Season={y}&Month=0&Day=0&Club={code}&Region=-1&Launchpoint=0&glider=0&pilot=0&turnpoint=&Noengines=false&sidx=FlightDate%20Desc,%20TPoints&sord=desc&skip=0&take=200 -> {data:[...], totalCount}. Bulk flat flight list, paginated, club-filterable. This is the JSON replacement for getlogfilescsv. QUIRK: sidx MUST include ', TPoints' or data returns null. Has ScoringDistance, XCPoints, Speed, HandicapSpeed, TP1-4/Start/Finish, ladder booleans, Site, Glider, Registration. LACKS TaskDistance, HandicapDistance, and the 'X% Completed' string.
2. /API/FLIGHT/{flightId} -> full per-flight detail (74 fields). Nested Task object has TaskDistance (declared task distance, the value flightCsvSpec.ts:142-150 currently reverse-engineers from the % string), plus TP_OK, Barrels (sector radii), ShapeFactor, SectorType. Also top-level SecondPilot and rich Glider (Seats/Turbo/Vintage). One request per flight.
3. /API/LADDERS/{year}/{ladder}/{club}/{ALL}/-1/false/false/false/false/false -> per-pilot aggregate (top-6 flights with FlightIDs).
CAM 2024 = 396 flights. TRADE-OFF: DAILYSCORESVIRTUAL alone is a clean CSV->JSON swap but drops the taskDistance source; getting exact TaskDistance/TP_OK/SecondPilot needs FLIGHT/{id} (~396 req/season) -> consider enriching lazily or caching.
close_reason: Done. Removed /api/flights proxy; CSV fetching+parsing moved client-side (src/lib/fetchFlights.ts via useFlights/SWR). Dropped axios + dead form-data override; moved csv.ts/flightCsvSpec.ts to src/lib (tests to test/lib). App is now purely client-side (no API routes). E2E mock switched to per-year BGA CSV fixtures; CLAUDE.md updated. Verified: 106 unit, 5 e2e, build, live-browser real-BGA fetch (CORS OK, correct winners, 0 console errors). CI green (check + e2e). Commits 16ccd43 + 6768627.

title: Add a season stats page (brainstorm UI from BGA ladder data first)
description:
Add a season stats page to the site (e.g. /stats?season=YYYY, linked from the home page).

FIRST STEP: brainstorm the stats page UI with the user before designing or building anything. The brainstorm should be driven by what the BGA Ladder flight data (getlogfilescsv) can support, not just by what the old scripts did.

Inputs for the brainstorm:
- The old ex-ladder-stats project (../ex-ladder-stats) produced club stats (completed/attempted counts per distance band, already shown by Stats.tsx) and per-pilot season totals of scoring km and cross-country points, exported as CSV for a spreadsheet (pilot_stats.js, lib/pilots.js, club_stats.js; example output cgc_pilots_2021.csv).
- The BGA CSV has 86 columns per flight; we currently parse only a subset (src/lib/flightCsvSpec.ts). Unparsed but potentially interesting: distance/speed/bonus/height points breakdown, scoring speed, task time, task shape (triangle/out-and-return etc.), start/finish/turnpoints and whether each was achieved, landout point, max height and height gain, junior/weekend/height ladder flags, turbo, competition flag, launch site, entry date.
- Fixture data gives a sense of scale: 2025 has ~400 club flights by ~49 pilots in ~62 gliders, ~86% launched from Gransden Lodge.

Open questions for the brainstorm:
- Audience: club members, committee/trophy admins, or both?
- Which flights count: all club flights (like ladders) or Gransden launches only; claimed ('C') flights only?
- Club-level vs per-pilot vs per-glider views; season-to-season comparisons.
- Tables vs charts (load the dataviz skill if charts are in scope); copy-to-spreadsheet export.

Implementation notes (after the brainstorm):
- Aggregations are sums/counts of CSV fields; no geometry or wgs84-util needed.
- Put aggregation in a pure, unit-tested src/lib module; reuse the season-boundary logic in eval.ts (inclusive UTC days).
- Easier after trophies-df3 (shared CopyButton/table components) and trophies-xsj (useFlights status union), but not blocked on them.
acceptance_criteria: A brainstorm with the user has agreed the stats page contents and layout (recorded in this bead's design field); the agreed page is implemented with unit-tested aggregation and e2e coverage.

title: Support clock-change season dates (Kelman Clock: last Sun Oct to last Sun Mar)
description:
The Kelman Clock period may change from fixed 1 Oct - 31 Mar to the UK clock changes (last Sunday of October to last Sunday of March), e.g. 25 Oct 2026 - 28 Mar 2027. Current blockers:
1. SeasonConfig (types.ts:27-30) only supports fixed {month, day}; add a rule such as {month, weekday: 'sun', nth: 'last'} (or a resolver) so dates are computed per season.
2. TrophyVersion (types.ts:39-44) only versions description/expr, so changing trophy.season would retroactively rescore past seasons. Allow history entries to carry 'season' so the old 1 Oct - 31 Mar range stays in force through its untilSeason (resolveTrophy already spreads overrides; mainly types + tests).
3. Boundary semantics: decide with the club whether the clock-change Sundays count. Likely: October Sunday inclusive (winter time starts that morning), March Sunday exclusive (summer time starts 01:00 that morning, so the season ends the Saturday before).
Cross-year seasons (start > end) already roll the end into the next year.
acceptance_criteria: Kelman Clock can be configured to the clock-change rule from a chosen season onward without changing results for earlier seasons; tests cover the computed dates for several years and both boundary days.
notes: Decision 2026-10-07 (from trophies-5in): fixing the boundary bug made Robert Theil (314.1 km, 31 Mar 2025) the computed 2024 Kelman Clock winner, but the trophy was already awarded to Andy Beatty (237.8 km, 15 Mar 2025) and that award stands. Once history entries can carry 'season', revisit whether to pin 2024 so the app shows the awarded result (e.g. via exclude or a 2024 season override). Note 31 Mar 2025 is after the 30 Mar 2025 clock change, so it would fall outside a clock-change season.

title: Accessibility pass on result tables and icons

Icon-only links lack accessible names (trophyDetail.tsx:126, admin.tsx:91, Settings link index.tsx:154). Tooltip.tsx is hover-only (add focus + aria-describedby). HeightLossWarning icon has no text alternative.

title: Typed CSV spec and clear error on missing columns

A renamed BGA column yields undefined and parseBoolean throws a confusing TypeError failing the whole fetch. Type the spec as a recursive discriminated union so output is checked against Flight; validate headers once and throw 'Missing CSV column "X"'.

title: Harden the turnpoints.ts generator pipeline
description: turnpoints.ts has no GENERATED header; source .cup isn't committed or recorded; update-turnpoints.py:24 ENTRY_RE only matches single-line entries, so if Biome wraps an entry the next run silently drops its added/removed metadata; turnpoints.test.ts:5 hard-codes count 1397. Emit header and exclude from Biome (or have script run biome format), fail on unparseable lines, record source URL/date, replace count with invariants (unique codes, removed only on retired codes).

title: Apply trophy exclude once before the DSL pipeline
description: eval.ts:104-114,142-148: every filter op re-checks flight.exclude and console.logs per excluded flight per filter; a trophy with no filter would keep excluded flights. Drop excluded flights once up front, keep the include bypass in filters, log once.

title: Type the trophy DSL expressions
description: types.ts:52 expr: any[][] means config typos (comparators, field paths, units) are only caught at runtime or not at all; trophyEval returns 'as ScoredFlight[]' regardless. Define an Expr union (filter/score/sort with typed comparators, a FlightPath union of used paths, units km|kph|pts, asc|desc), apply to Trophy and TrophyVersion, drop any callbacks. Keep the intentional score->sort fall-through. First add unit tests for filter/score/sort, '<=>', include/exclude.

title: Season picker can step past its bounds
description: Season.tsx:26,38 disables prev/next with season === firstYear / === currentYear, so ?season=1990 or ?season=2099 lets you step forever. Use <= / >= (or clamp). Optionally split into a controlled SeasonPicker + URL-bound wrapper and reuse it in components.tsx:309-342, which hand-rolls a copy.

title: Set "type": "module" in package.json
description: Vite warns that vite.config.ts uses ESM syntax in a file loaded as CommonJS; configLoader 'native' will become the default in a future Vite major. Fix: add "type": "module" to package.json. Requires migrating CommonJS usages: e2e/helpers.ts (__dirname -> import.meta.dirname) and scripts/add-milestone.ts (require/__dirname -> ESM imports). Verify lint, tests, e2e, build, and Netlify build.
notes: Also modernise scripts/add-milestone.ts: ESM imports instead of require (drop stale eslint-disable), fix usage text (still says npx ts-node), escape the milestone value used to build a RegExp (line ~36).

title: Raise test coverage to the next 10% threshold (and enforce it)
description: After the Vitest migration (trophies-8g1) establishes a coverage baseline, write tests to reach the next 10% milestone and add an enforced coverage threshold at that level in vitest config (so it ratchets up rather than the old unmet 100%). Currently ~38% lines / 2% statements over all source (only src/lib logic is tested; hooks/stats/fetchFlights/pages/components untested). Target the highest-value untested logic first (e.g. stats.ts, fetchFlights, useFlights).

Enforced 80% global threshold in vite.config.ts (verified it fails when unmet). 146 tests pass; lint + build green.

title: Allow the trophies config file to be specified explicitly (e.g. via env var)
description: Currently trophies.config.ts at the project root is imported statically (import config from '../../trophies.config') across the client code. Add a way to point the app at a different config file — e.g. a TROPHIES_CONFIG env var giving a path — so the app can run for different clubs without editing the tracked config. CONSTRAINT: the config is a statically-imported TS module bundled into the client, so a plain runtime env var can't switch files; this needs build-time resolution (e.g. a Turbopack/webpack module alias driven by the env var, a config-loader indirection, or a small prebuild step that resolves the path). Design around that. Relates to the documented 'adapt this app for a different gliding club' goal.
close_reason: Added TROPHIES_CONFIG build-time config selection via a Vite resolve.alias ('trophies-config' -> process.env.TROPHIES_CONFIG, default trophies.config.ts). All 7 imports use the alias; tsconfig paths keeps tsc resolving it; Vitest inherits the alias. Verified override swaps the bundled config (sentinel test) and default build unchanged; lint/tsc/146 unit/build/5 e2e green. Committed d837456.

title: Align @types/node with the pinned Node 24 LTS

Action: pin @types/node to ^24 and add a renovate.json packageRule so @types/node follows the Node major we run (allowedVersions / matchPackageNames) rather than latest. Avoids type/runtime drift.
close_reason: Done. Pinned @types/node to ^24 (24.13.2) to match the Node 24 LTS runtime (was ^25; Renovate proposed v26). Added a renovate.json rule capping @types/node at <25 so it tracks the Node major. Verified: tsc --noEmit exit 0, lint clean; CI green (check + e2e). Commit ce9f110.

title: Evaluate Babel 7 -> 8 major upgrade
description: From Renovate Dependency Dashboard (#1): major bump of the babel monorepo to v8 (@babel/core, @babel/preset-env, @babel/preset-react, @babel/runtime). Babel 8 is a breaking major used by babel-jest + the next/babel preset, and it interacts with our @babel/core ^7.29.7 security override. Action: test the Jest suite + build under babel 8 on a branch; if not ready, add a renovate.json packageRule to hold the babel monorepo at v7 so the dashboard stops re-proposing it.
close_reason: Evaluated: Babel 7->8 upgrade is moot. @babel/runtime (devDep) and @babel/core (override) were unused Next.js/Jest leftovers — @babel/core wasn't even in the lockfile; plugin-react@6 uses oxc not Babel. Removed both (fafa0df). Only @babel/parser+types remain transitively via magicast at v7. Clean install + lint + 146 unit + build + 5/5 e2e all pass. Renovate will drop the v8 proposal on next scan; no hold-rule needed.

title: Evaluate JSON-only fields (SecondPilot, Seats/Turbo/Vintage) for trophy accuracy
description: The JSON flight detail exposes fields the CSV lacks: top-level SecondPilot, and Glider.Seats/Turbo/Vintage. Evaluate whether these improve trophy correctness — e.g. SecondPilot for genuine two-crew detection (vs the Complicity Cup's current registration-grouping + minPilots>=2 heuristic), and Seats/Turbo/Vintage for fleet/class-based trophies. Deliverable: decide which trophies benefit and update trophies.config.ts/eval.ts accordingly. Blocked by trophies-ouv.
close_reason: Won't do. No current trophy is incorrect for lack of these JSON-only fields. (1) SecondPilot doesn't improve the Complicity Cup — that's a syndicate ladder (best 6 scores per glider registration, >=2 distinct pilots across the season); registration-grouping + minPilots>=2 is the correct model. SecondPilot is single-flight second crew, a different concept, and no two-crew/two-seat trophy exists. (2) No vintage/turbo/seats trophy exists; the only class trophy (L6 Bolly/ASW19) already works via a glider-type regex, and class/fleet grouping otherwise rides on CSV ladder flags. All these fields are JSON-only, so obtaining them requires the per-flight FLIGHT/{id} enrichment declined in trophies-ouv. Re-file with a concrete trophy if the club ever adds a Vintage/two-seat/Turbo award.

title: Drop task-distance %-parsing hack via /API/FLIGHT/{id} enrichment
description: flightCsvSpec.ts:142-150 reverse-engineers the declared task distance by parsing 'X% Completed' out of the Task Achievement text and dividing scoringDistance by it. The JSON /API/FLIGHT/{id} endpoint exposes Task.TaskDistance directly (plus TP_OK, Barrels, ShapeFactor, SectorType, SecondPilot, and richer Glider: Seats/Turbo/Vintage). Enrich each flight via FLIGHT/{id} and remove the percentage hack. Cost: ~1 request per flight (CAM ~396/season) — do it lazily/cached or only for flights that feed trophies. Blocked by trophies-grb (JSON data source).
close_reason: Won't do. Same rationale as parent trophies-grb (JSON migration declined — CSV stays the data source). taskDistanceKm only feeds coarse 100km-wide stats buckets in stats.ts, not any trophy scoring. The % Completed hack (flightCsvSpec.ts) recovers task distance to within rounding error, captures decimals, and falls back to scoringDistanceKm for completed/missing-pct flights. Not worth ~396 per-flight FLIGHT/{id} requests + caching to refine a cosmetic stat. Hack documented in-code.

title: Evaluate migrating Next.js -> Vite + React (static SPA)
description: Once /api/flights is removed (trophies-xeh) the app has no server-side code at all, so Next.js is only acting as a static bundler. Evaluate moving to Vite + React (+ a lightweight router like React Router/wouter). The bulk of the code (eval.ts, csv parsing, stats.ts, trophies.config.ts, types) is framework-agnostic plain TS and ports as-is; only the handful of Pages-Router pages are Next-specific. Cheaper alternative to compare against: keep Next with output:'export' for a static build (near-zero work). Decision should fold in the bun migration (trophies-sz2), since Vite + bun is a natural combo. Deliverable: a recommendation (Vite vs Next static export) with rough effort estimate.
close_reason: Done. Migrated Next.js -> Vite + React Router. App is a pure client-side SPA (src/main.tsx BrowserRouter, src/App.tsx routes: /, /trophy/:trophyId, /admin, /components, catch-all -> /). Replaced next/router->useSearchParams/useParams, next/link->RR Link, next/dynamic->direct import; renamed [trophyId].tsx->trophyDetail.tsx; Tailwind via @tailwindcss/vite; jest next/babel preset->@babel/preset-env+react+typescript. Removed next, next.config.js, postcss.config.mjs, _app.tsx, next-env.d.ts, @tailwindcss/postcss. Verified: vite build, 112 unit, tsc, biome, 5 e2e (Vite build), live-browser (real BGA renders, client routing + catch-all, 0 console errors); CI green. Commit 3d77e49.
